text:
Incident Bot: PagerDuty alert triggered -> P1: sustained p95 latency spike for /v1/stream in us-west-2 (3x baseline). Auto-escalation to incidents channel.
Jordan (oncall): I'm on it. Seeing queue depth jump on the streaming workers, KV cache thrash, a bunch of token timeouts in the logs. Non-streaming generate endpoints look OK.
Priya Nair: If streaming is the only path failing, we should consider an immediate temporary pause of streaming push frames (SSE) for affected region to reduce tail latency and restore throughput.
Jordan (oncall): Agreed. Will coordinate a controlled pause and fallback plan. Any objections?
Alex Chen: I can run the toggle. Runbook reference: runbooks/streaming-mitigation (link). We have a console toggle and an infra API; I'll use infra CLI so it's auditable.
Alex Chen: Running command now:
```
# disable streaming in us-west-2 for the public endpoint
infra toggle-streaming --region=usw2 --state=off --reason="P1 latency mitigation" --ticket=INC-1933
```
Deploy Bot: rollout triggered by Alex Chen. Change ID: r-cc12f.
Deploy Bot: streaming feature flag set -> off for region=usw2 (started at 2026-03-15T15:22:10Z).
Jordan (oncall): Paused. Confirming fallback behavior: clients should get HTTP 200 + final chunk with reason header and then be served via non-streaming generate path where possible.
Maya (sre): I'm watching metrics. Initial signal: p95 for /v1/stream dropped from ~2.4s to ~0.9s within 60s of pause. Worker queue depth down 65%. CPU on the host pool is back to normal.
Customer Success - Ben: We have two enterprise customers on Dedicated who use streaming heavily (AcmeCorp, FinX). Do we need to notify them?
Priya Nair: Notify high-touch customers immediately and post an update to status.redwood.ai. Use template "temporary streaming pause - mitigation". CS Ben to send targeted DM.
Customer Success - Ben: noted, sending DMs and creating a status update.
Jordan (oncall): Short-term follow-ups: 1) keep streaming paused in usw2, 2) tighten burst quota for anonymous public clients to prevent spike re-ingress, 3) scale up a small additional streaming pool if metrics demand.
Alex Chen: Tightening quotas: applying rate-limit rule now to public keys in usw2 to 10r/s top-level burst=50. Command:
```
infra rate-limit update --region=usw2 --scope=public --rps=10 --burst=50 --reason="post-mitigation hardening"
```
Deploy Bot: rate-limit update applied (rule rl-9a3f).
Maya (sre): After quota change, background noise dropped further, p95 for all endpoints stable. No error spike on generate. We'll keep an eye on error-rate for clients expected to fallback to polling.
Jordan (oncall): Handoff time. My shift ends in 25min. Maya, can you take on incident lead and run the re-enable canary plan once we have stable metrics for 15m?
Maya (sre): Taking lead. Plan: re-enable streaming in canary -> 2% traffic for 10m -> 20% for 10m -> 100% if healthy. If p95 climbs >1.5x baseline, rollback to off.
Priya Nair: Also add a temporary policy to prefer low-latency model variants and smaller max_tokens for streaming requests while canary is ongoing. That should reduce KV pressure.
Alex Chen: I'll prepare the canary job and document the rollback steps. Dump of relevant logs pulled to the incident ticket: /incidents/1933054321/logs.tar.gz
Incident Bot: Incident ticket updated -> INC-1933. Current severity P1.
Customer Success - Ben: status.redwood.ai posted, enterprise DMs sent, customers acknowledge.
Maya (sre): Monitoring note: watching p50/p95 CPU, worker queue, kv-cache hit-rate, and egress token timeouts. Next update in 10m or on any change.
Jordan (oncall): Thanks all - handing off formally to Maya. If anyone needs to join the canary window, ping @here.
Maya (sre): Acknowledged. I'll post a short postmortem skeleton after the incident stabilizes.
Alex Chen: Will keep the audit logs and the infra toggles attached to INC-1933.
Jordan (oncall): Off shift now. Good job team. :thumbsup:
Maya (sre): Update 10m later -> canary job scheduled, metrics green. Proceeding with 20% ramp in 5m.
Maya (sre): Update 25m later -> 20% stable. No regressions. Queues remain normal. Planning full re-enable in 15m with rollback ready.
Maya (sre): Full re-enable completed. Monitoring for 10m.
Maya (sre): Final update -> system stable, incident closing. Root cause investigation TBD (likely KV cache thrash + surging streaming fanout). Postmortem to follow.
Incident Bot: Incident INC-1933 status -> resolved (2026-03-15T16:02:00Z).
